full_judgment:
24. The statement of PW 2 deserves credence as is more consistent with ordinary course of events that naturally follows in the peculiar circumstances. It is natural, in the peculiar circumstances, that the brother living at home would take care of the properties of the absentee brother and would do all acts of the real owner i.e., the act of possession, cultivation, letting out to tenants, paying rent etc. The possession of one brother does not per se raise any presumption in favour of benami transaction as against the other. It is the nature of relationship between the parties and other attend-ant facts and circumstances that indicate the underlying sense of the possession and of the nature of transaction. 

 "It is well established that where there is a clear picture as to source of passing consideration in a transaction, long and continued possession of the parties trying to set up benami though an important element for consideration does not raise any presumption in favour of benami" 

 29. It is now well settled that claim of benami transaction, for success, must be brought home by convincing evidence as to some basic elements of such transaction, such as, motive of purchase, source of money of the beneficial owner, custody of title documents and conduct of the parties in relation to the land, Mere possession, if any, of the suit land does not ipso facto raise any presumption in favour of benami transaction. Someone from outside the deed must take heavier burden to dislodge the general presumption in favour of the apparent vendees of the deed.
